# Cade

> A small, durable coding agent built on one append-only session log.

# Cade

<!-- source: README.md -->

# Cade

Cade is a standalone coding agent. It keeps one rule at the center of the
design:

> The session log is the source of truth. The model-visible history is a
> deterministic projection. Request construction only produces the current
> request.

The result is a small agent that can survive compaction, window changes, and
process restarts without inventing history.

Chinese translations of the current guides start at [中文文档](zh/README.md).

## Built docs

The docs are Markdown-first. A small tool validates links and anchors, builds a
single-page site, and generates an `llms.txt` catalog for agents:

```bash
uv run --locked python -m cade.docs check
uv run --locked --extra docs python -m cade.docs build
uv run --locked python -m cade.docs llms --write
uv run --locked python -m cade.docs catalogs --write
```

The generated site is [docs/index.html](index.html); the generated
catalogs are `docs/llms.txt`, `docs/llms-full.txt`, and the
config, event, and module pages under `design/`.

# Quickstart

<!-- source: quickstart.md -->

# Quickstart

Cade requires Python 3.12 or newer. The repository uses `uv` for
development and for the `cade` entry point.

## Install and authenticate

From the repository root:

```bash
uv sync --locked
```

Cade owns its credential store at `~/.cade/auth.json`. Log in with
Sign in with ChatGPT (SIWC) in a browser:

```bash
uv run --locked cade login
```

The browser flow registers Cade on first use and reuses that registration
on later sign-ins. It stores a stable host ID at `~/.cade/host.json`. SIWC
has no device-code flow. On a headless host, complete the login locally, copy
`auth.json`, and let the remote host create its own host ID on the next login.
Or use an API key.

For an OpenAI API key, use a hidden key prompt or set the environment variable:

```bash
uv run --locked cade login --provider openai
export OPENAI_API_KEY=...
uv run --locked cade --provider openai --model gpt-5.5 -p "Review this project."
```

DeepSeek uses the same Responses protocol with its own API key:

```bash
uv run --locked cade login --provider deepseek
export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=...
uv run --locked cade --provider deepseek --model deepseek-flash -p "Review this project."
```

The default provider is `chatgpt`. Set `provider` and `model` in
`cade.json` to choose other startup defaults. Cade supports only the
Responses protocol: `chatgpt` for ChatGPT plan usage, `openai` for an OpenAI
API key, and `deepseek` for a DeepSeek API key. State from the earlier Cade
project is not compatible; use clean `~/.cade/` and workspace `.cade/`
directories.

## Run one task

```bash
uv run --locked cade -p "Read README.md and explain the entry point in three bullets."
```

The same command can be written explicitly:

```bash
uv run --locked cade exec "Read README.md and explain the entry point."
```

Cade runs in the current directory by default. Use `--project-root` to
point at another workspace.

## Choose a mode

- `build` is the default. Normal edits, tests, builds, and shell pipelines run
  automatically; detected risky operations ask.
- `ask` allows classified read-only operations and asks before changes or
  unclassified shell commands.
- `plan` hides write and edit tools and denies mutations. Read-only shell
  commands are allowed.

```bash
uv run --locked cade --mode plan -p "Propose a fix for the failing test."
uv run --locked cade --mode build -p "Fix the bug and run the test."
```

For non-interactive automation, `--yes` approves asks, and `--read-only` denies
mutations while allowing classified read-only shell commands. Prefer rule-based allows over `--yes` for shared
repositories; see [Configuration](configuration.md).

## Continue work

Sessions live under `.cade/sessions` by default.

```bash
uv run --locked cade --list-sessions
uv run --locked cade --continue -p "What did you change?"
uv run --locked cade --resume SESSION_ID -p "Continue the task."
```

Run `cade` to start the inline TUI. `cade "Review this project."` starts the TUI
and sends the task as its first message, then stays open. See [CLI](cli.md) for interactive
commands and [Hosts](hosts.md) for key bindings.

## Build the docs

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra docs
uv run --locked python -m cade.docs check
uv run --locked python -m cade.docs build
```

Open `docs/index.html`. The docs source is under `docs/`.

# CLI

<!-- source: cli.md -->

# CLI

The `cade` entry point runs one task, starts an interactive terminal host,
or manages sessions.

```bash
cade [TASK] [options]
cade -p TASK [options]
cade exec TASK [options]
```

`cade` starts the TUI in an interactive terminal. An optional positional task
is sent as its first message; the TUI stays open afterward. Use `-p TASK`
(or `--prompt TASK`) or `exec TASK` to run one task and exit. The positional
TUI prompt and `-p` cannot be combined.

## Login

```bash
cade login
cade login --provider openai
cade login --provider deepseek
```

`--provider` defaults to `chatgpt`, which uses Sign in with ChatGPT (SIWC)
in a browser. `openai` and `deepseek` use `api_key` with a hidden input prompt.
Credentials are stored in `~/.cade/auth.json`; the stable SIWC host ID is
stored in `~/.cade/host.json`. Login does not change project provider or
model settings. Cade supports only the Responses protocol. ChatGPT login
and OpenAI API keys expose the registered OpenAI chat model pool through separate
authentication routes. A refreshable OAuth token still makes models selectable;
the provider refreshes it when needed.

## One-shot options

- `-p TASK` / `--prompt TASK` runs one task and exits, like `cade exec TASK`.

- `--project-root PATH` sets the workspace. The default is the current
  directory.
- `--config PATH` selects a config file. The default is
  `<project-root>/cade.json`.
- `--provider NAME`, `--model NAME`, and `--effort EFFORT` override provider
  defaults.
- `--mode plan|build|ask` selects the work mode. Default is `build`.
- `--sandbox read-only|workspace-write|danger-full-access` selects filesystem
  scope. Default is `workspace-write`; Windows skips OS confinement.
- `--network` / `--no-network` controls sandbox networking. Default is enabled.
- `--read-only` / `--no-read-only` controls mutation denial. Read-only shell
  commands remain available.
- `--yes` approves asks. Use it only in trusted, non-interactive contexts.
- `--auto-review` / `--no-auto-review` lets the model review ask-level calls.
- `--max-steps N` bounds model steps.
- `--context-window N` overrides the model context window. It is required for
  models that are not in the built-in registry.
- `--json` emits JSONL events for a one-shot task.
- `--steer TEXT` injects guidance at the next model step of a one-shot task;
  repeatable.

## Sessions

- `--list-sessions` prints ID, update time, and title, then exits.
- `--continue` resumes the latest session in the project.
- `--resume` resumes the latest session; `--resume ID` resumes a specific one.
- `--sessions-dir PATH` changes the session directory. A relative path is
  resolved against the project root.
- `--undo` reverses one checkpoint action in the latest session and exits without
  contacting a provider or starting MCP. Use `--resume ID --undo` to select a
  session. It uses the same conversation and file recovery as TUI `/undo`.

`--continue` and `--resume` cannot be combined. Session listings and automatic
continuation skip conversations without a nonempty user message. New interactive
sessions keep setup records in memory until the first user or assistant message;
opening the TUI or running `/new` alone creates no session file. Existing files
are not automatically deleted.

## Goals

- `--goal TEXT` sets the workspace goal before running.

## Interactive commands

The TUI accepts these slash commands and provides native selectors for models,
modes, configuration, and permissions.

- `/new` starts a new session. `/clear` is an alias and keeps saved conversations.
- `/continue` opens the same saved-conversation picker as `/sessions`.
- `/resume` opens the saved-conversation picker; `/resume ID` resumes that session.
- `/sessions` opens the same picker as `/resume`.
- `/tree [ENTRY]` navigates the full history tree within the same session.
  Selecting a user input restores it for editing; other entries continue after
  the selected point. The position survives restart and old branches remain.
- `/fork [N|ENTRY]` copies history before a user turn into a new session and puts
  that input in the editor. It can select inactive branches; `N=1` selects the
  latest recorded input. Files stay unchanged.
- `/clone` copies only the active path to a new session and clears the editor.
- `/undo` reverses one user turn or explicit recovery action. `/redo` reapplies
  one undone action without contacting the model or rerunning tools.
- `/rewind` selects an active-path user prompt and offers conversation, code, or
  both. `/rewind ENTRY conversation|code|both` selects the scope directly, then
  opens the confirmation preview.
- `/revert` selects a turn range and all or one tracked file without trimming
  conversation. `/revert START [END] -- PATH ...` selects multiple files; quote
  paths containing spaces and use forward slashes. END is inclusive; omitting it
  includes the latest action. Conflicting later edits block restoration.
- `/compact [INSTRUCTIONS]` summarizes older turns and applies optional guidance.
- `/model [PROVIDER/MODEL]` switches an exact authenticated model or searches the
  model picker for a partial name.
- `/effort [LEVEL]` chooses a model reasoning effort or opens its picker.
- `/thinking [LEVEL]` selects reasoning effort. Use `Ctrl+T` to fold reasoning
  output without changing effort.
- `/verbose [low|medium|high]` controls interactive TUI display detail. It
  starts in `low`: assistant messages stay visible, while thinking and tool
  transcripts are hidden. `medium` shows collapsed thinking and tool summaries;
  `high` expands both. Without an argument, the command opens a picker. The
  choice affects display only, including restored history; it does not change
  requests, tool execution, or the saved session. `Ctrl+T` and `Ctrl+O` still
  offer manual folding. The setting applies to the running TUI, not headless
  execution.
- `/rollover [--force]` starts a new context window; `/new-context` is an alias.
- `/new-context [--force]` starts a new context window using `NOTE.md` as the
  handoff. Write that file first, or use `--force` to reset without it.
- `/mode [MODE]` shows or switches the execution mode.
- `/permissions [list|clear]` lists or clears session grants; without arguments it opens a picker.
- `/goal [TEXT|done|clear]` shows, sets, completes, or clears the goal.
- `/context-window [SIZE|default]` shows or changes the current context window.
- `/context` shows estimated context usage, source totals, remaining input space, and loaded
  file paths with token estimates, including instructions, skills, MCP schemas,
  and loaded MCP content. OpenAI API-key totals use its input-count API;
  ChatGPT plan sessions use local estimates because SIWC does not document an
  input-count endpoint. DeepSeek uses
  its official V4 text tokenizer with estimated request overhead. Last-request
  provider usage is shown separately.
- `/btw QUESTION` asks an independent side question.
- `/steer TEXT` queues guidance for the next model step.
- `/queue [followup|steer|interrupt|TEXT]` chooses how busy `Enter` behaves, or queues TEXT for the next turn.
- `/stop` interrupts a pending model request, including the wait for its first
  output. Tools stop at their cancellation checks.
- `/help` prints the command list.
- `/auth [status|login|logout]` displays authentication status or routes to login/logout.
- `/login` selects an authentication method and provider. `/logout` removes a
  selected stored credential, not environment variables.
- `/connect` selects a provider and opens its model picker after authentication.
- `/skill [NAME]` activates a skill for the next task.
- `/tool [list]` shows available tools and their descriptions.
- `/config [KEY[=VALUE]]` browses settings or updates a project setting.
- `/memory` shows the workspace memory file path.
- `/exit` or `/quit` exits.

The TUI does not register `/rename` or `/mcp`. Recovery changes tracked files,
not arbitrary shell effects, external services, or the user's Git index.
See [recovery coverage and conflicts](snapshots-goals.md#checkpoint-recovery).
`--undo` cannot be combined with a task; both undo entry points use the same
persistent action history.

## Interactive input

- `@path` attaches a workspace file to the task.
- `$skill` loads a skill body into the task.
- `!command` runs a shell command without contacting the model. Permission
  checks still apply.

```text
Review @src/cade/harness/loop.py and use $review-only
!git status
```

During a task, the TUI keeps reading input:

- `/steer TEXT` appends guidance at the next model step.
- `/queue TEXT` runs TEXT after the current task.
- `/stop` or `Esc` interrupts the task without waiting for the next model
  output. Undelivered queued inputs return to the editor with any current draft.
- `Ctrl+C` clears the editor without interrupting the task. Press it again
  within 500 ms to exit.
- Other text is queued as a follow-up task.

When idle with empty input, press `Esc` twice within 500 ms to open `/rewind`.
Tree navigation, fork, and clone do not restore workspace files.
Inside a picker or form, `Esc` closes that interaction instead. Clearing input
with `Ctrl+C` is separate from cancelling a task with `Esc`.

Steering is applied between steps, not inside a provider stream or a running
tool. See [Steering and queueing](design/steering-queue.md).

## Exit codes

- `0`: the run completed.
- `1`: the run ended without completion, or `--undo` found no session or action
  or could not apply recovery.
- `2`: argument, configuration, or startup error.
- `130`: login was cancelled.

## Examples

```bash
cade --list-sessions
cade --continue -p "Summarize the current state."
cade --undo
cade --mode plan -p "Find the smallest fix for the failing test."
cade --mode build --yes -p "Fix the test and run pytest."
```

# Configuration

<!-- source: configuration.md -->

# Configuration

Cade reads `<project-root>/cade.json` by default. Use `--config PATH`
to select another file. Command-line options override the file; the file
overrides built-in defaults.

The file is strict: unknown keys and invalid values are rejected instead of
silently ignored.

In the TUI, `/config` opens a settings browser. Every setting opens an arrow-key
menu with the current value selected. Numeric settings offer presets; nullable
settings offer **Use default**. Choose **Custom value...** to enter an arbitrary
number, path, or model name in a prefilled form. Press Enter to save or Esc to
return to the choices. Saved defaults take effect on the next start.

## Example

```json
{
  "provider": "chatgpt",
  "model": "gpt-5.6-luna",
  "reasoning_effort": "high",
  "context_window": 128000,
  "max_steps": 30,
  "sessions_dir": ".cade/sessions",
  "mode": "build",
  "sandbox": "workspace-write",
  "network": true,
  "read_only": false,
  "instructions": true,
  "note": true,
  "memory": true,
  "auto_review": false,
  "prompt_modules": ["identity", "tool_discipline", "working_note", "environment"],
  "rules": [
    {
      "tool": "bash",
      "command_prefix": "git status",
      "decision": "allow"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Fields

- `provider`, `model`: provider name and model identifier. Use `chatgpt`
  for ChatGPT plan usage (Sign in with ChatGPT), `openai` for an OpenAI API
  key, or `deepseek` for a DeepSeek API key. The CLI flags override both.
- `reasoning_effort`: provider reasoning effort. The CLI flag is `--effort`.
- `context_window`: model context window in tokens. The default comes from the
  registered model metadata. Unregistered models require this field or
  `--context-window`; Cade rejects them otherwise.
- `max_steps`: maximum model steps in one run.
- `sessions_dir`: session directory. Relative paths resolve against the project
  root.
- `mode`: `plan`, `build`, or `ask`. Default is `build`; replace old `act` values with `ask`.
- `sandbox`: `read-only`, `workspace-write` (default), or `danger-full-access`.
  Windows skips OS confinement regardless of this setting.
- `network`: allow tool network access. Default is true. OS enforcement of false
  for shell commands requires Linux/macOS confinement. Web tools reject calls
  on every platform when this is false.
- Web search uses Exa. Set `EXA_API_KEY` to supply your own key; it is optional.
  Remove the obsolete `websearch_provider` field from existing `cade.json` files.
- `read_only`: deny mutations and allow only classified read-only shell commands.
- `instructions`: load `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` into request context.
- `note`: load `NOTE.md` working state.
- `memory`: load `MEMORY.md` durable facts.
- `auto_review`: let the model review ask-level tool calls. Default is false.
- `prompt_modules`: system prompt modules. Available names are `identity`,
  `tool_discipline`, `working_note`, and `environment`.

## Rules

Rules match a tool name or `*`, optionally a normalized path subtree or command
prefix. All matches participate: `deny` takes precedence over `ask`, then
`allow`. Order does not matter. `allow` overrides mode defaults, not an effective
explicit deny.

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {"tool": "bash", "command_prefix": "git", "decision": "deny"},
    {"tool": "bash", "command_prefix": "git status", "decision": "allow"},
    {"tool": "write", "path_prefix": "docs/", "decision": "allow"}
  ]
}
```

In this example, `git status` is denied because the broader deny still matches.
Remove or narrow that deny to allow it. Plan constraints, protected paths, and
`read_only` win over grants and rules. External writes request additional
permissions instead of being unconditionally denied. See
[Tools and security](tools-security.md) for scopes and approval behavior.

## MCP servers

MCP servers use stdio or Streamable HTTP and keep one connection per server.

```json
{
  "mcp_servers": {
    "files": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["mcp_server.py"],
      "cwd": ".",
      "timeout_ms": 30000,
      "env": {"LOG_LEVEL": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

Discovered tools are exposed as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. They ask by default,
are denied in plan mode and read-only mode, and can be allowed by a rule.

Use `env` for ordinary process settings and `env_from` to pass named host
environment variables to a stdio server. Only the SDK's basic process environment
is inherited; other host credentials are not copied automatically. For HTTP,
use `headers_from` to load request headers from host environment variables:

```json
{
  "mcp_servers": {
    "remote": {
      "transport": "streamable-http",
      "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
      "headers_from": {"Authorization": "EXAMPLE_MCP_AUTH"},
      "timeout_ms": 30000
    }
  }
}
```

Set `EXAMPLE_MCP_AUTH` outside Cade to the complete authorization header value.
Store credentials in your environment or external secret manager, not project
configuration, URLs, command arguments, or skill files. Cade does not persist a
credential cache; explicitly passed credential values are redacted from MCP
results and diagnostics. MCP server processes are trusted extensions outside
the workspace tool sandbox, so configure only servers you trust.

Set `trust_project_skills: true` to discover project skills. `skills_dir` selects
an additional trusted directory relative to the project root or by absolute
path. See [Skills and memory](skills-memory.md).

# Architecture

<!-- source: architecture.md -->

# Architecture

Cade is a standalone coding agent in `src/cade/`. It uses a pipeline
with four stages. Each stage has one owner and one direction of data flow.

```text
Session log -> Conversation projection -> Request -> Run
```

## Session log

`SessionLog` is an append-only JSONL file. Each entry has an ID, timestamp,
type, parent ID, and data. The active branch ends at the latest entry. `/tree`
appends a navigation event whose parent identifies the continuation point;
alternatives remain in the same file. The loop follows only that active path.

The log stores facts:

- `system`, `user`, `assistant`, and `tool_result` are model-visible facts.
- `compaction` records a summary and `first_kept_id`.
- `window` records a new context start and an optional handoff.
- `request`, `run`, `attempt`, `branch`, `checkpoint`, and `restore` are audit facts. They never become
  conversation messages. A branch event also preserves a selected input for
  editing after restart.

The schema is closed. See [Session log schema](reference/session-schema.md).

## Projection

`project(entries)` is a pure function. It reads the branch and produces the
deterministic conversation projection:

1. Take the latest system message.
2. Apply the latest window start.
3. Apply the latest compaction summary.
4. Keep retained user, assistant, and tool-result messages.
5. Pair tool calls with tool results; insert a synthetic interrupted result at
   the tail when the log ends mid-call.

No projection step writes to the log. Replaying the same entries always
produces the same conversation.

## Request

`build(conversation, tools, budget, context)` admits messages into the current
model window. It:

- joins request-only context such as instructions, skill catalog, NOTE, memory,
  and goal;
- preserves every projected message and tool result;
- checks the complete request against the input budget;
- converts the result to provider wire format;
- returns a `Request` with a `BuildReport`.

Admission does not mutate the conversation and does not write facts. Only
compaction and window events change the visible history. An over-budget request
is rejected rather than silently truncated.

## Run

Before appending a new user fact, `run()` persists interrupted results for
unfinished tool calls. It does not repeat tools whose outcome is unknown.
It then calls the provider, appends assistant and tool-result facts, and executes
tools. It is the only stage that writes during a turn. Compaction and window
fallback are decisions expressed as new log facts.

## Package boundaries

Cade has five runtime packages:

- `ai`: model protocols, providers, model metadata, and authentication protocols.
- `harness`: the log-driven agent loop, session facts and projections, request
  admission, tool execution contracts, and internal execution backends.
- `coding`: programming tools, project context, workspace policy, subagents,
  MCP integration, snapshots, and coordinated workspace recovery.
- `app`: configuration, credentials, provider assembly, application sessions,
  settings, and commands.
- `hosts`: CLI arguments, terminal I/O, and TUI presentation.

Dependencies point from hosts to app, coding, harness, and AI. Each layer may
use lower layers; lower layers never import higher layers. The harness includes
agent runtime behavior; there is no parallel agent package. Local process and
sandbox implementations live inside `harness/execution/local`, not at the
package root. Execution scope contracts do not import those platform backends.
`tests/test_architecture.py` checks these boundaries.

`app/bootstrap.py` creates the same `ApplicationSession` for one-shot and TUI
execution. `app/session.py` owns active-session operations; it does not import
terminal modules. `harness/executor.py` handles authorization, per-call scope,
timeouts, and tool errors for both model calls and direct application calls.
The loop remains responsible for recording model-turn facts and emits completed
tool events after recording results.

See the [code map](design/code-map.md) for implementation locations. Cade does
not depend on the earlier Cade project and provides no compatibility import
paths. Import types and functions from their owning modules.

## Recovery

Application assembly injects a `TurnLifecycle` into the harness loop. It creates a root-turn
checkpoint before the user fact, links it after that fact, and closes it after
execution. Tool workers and synchronous subagents inherit capture ownership.
The harness does not import the workspace store. Recovery serializes cooperating
writers with a workspace lock in addition to the session run lock.

The native snapshot store retains both file images. An append-only workspace
action journal drives stepwise undo/redo; the session log remains authoritative
for conversation ancestry. A durable pending plan coordinates files and the
conversation commit. Recovery resumes idempotently after interruption and stops
on unknown external edits. See [Snapshots and goals](snapshots-goals.md).

## Lower layers and state

`ai/` owns provider protocols, streaming adapters, model metadata, and OAuth.
`harness/execution/` owns execution scopes, local process execution, and output
capture. Neither AI nor the harness imports application or host modules. The AI layer supports only the Responses
protocol, as recorded in [decision 0007](decisions/0007-responses-only-provider.md),
and uses Sign in with ChatGPT for plan usage, as recorded in
[decision 0008](decisions/0008-siwc-login.md). DeepSeek uses a separate
transport with the same Responses stream format and its own endpoint.
`harness/execution/local/sandbox.py` owns bubblewrap and Seatbelt process wrapping.
`harness/permissions.py` carries structured approval results and per-call scopes.
The CLI confines shell and file workers on Linux/macOS; Windows runs directly.
See [Tools and security](tools-security.md) for boundaries and trusted extensions.

Credentials and user skills use `~/.cade/`. The SIWC host ID lives in
`~/.cade/host.json`. Sessions, snapshots, goals,
and project skills use `<workspace>/.cade/`. Project settings live in
`cade.json`. The earlier Cade project's state formats are not compatible with
this project; start from clean `~/.cade/` and workspace `.cade/` directories.

See the [code map](design/code-map.md) and
[persistence catalog](design/persistence-catalog.md) for implementation locations
and durable state ownership.

## Why the split

The split prevents a common failure: the request builder starts hiding
messages, then the history rewrite becomes the only copy of what happened. Cade
keeps the original facts and lets the projection and admission be replaced
without losing history.

# Sessions and context

<!-- source: sessions-context.md -->

# Sessions and context

A session is an append-only JSONL file under `.cade/sessions` by default.
The file name is `session-<id>.jsonl`. The session title is derived from the
first user message; no extra event type is needed.

On POSIX, new session directories use mode `0700` and log files use `0600`.
Opening an existing log tightens that file to `0600`; existing directory
permissions stay unchanged. Windows inherits directory ACLs. Logs contain full
request inputs, so choose a private directory for custom session storage.

## Resume

```bash
cade --list-sessions
cade --continue "Continue where we stopped."
cade --resume SESSION_ID "Explain the current state."
```

`--continue` and `--resume` open the latest or a specific session. Existing
sessions keep their original system fact; a new `cade.json` does not rewrite
history. If a resumed session has no system entry, the current prompt is added.

## Tree, fork, and clone

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `/tree [ENTRY]` | Switch position within the same session, preserving all branches |
| `/fork [N\|ENTRY]` | Copy history before a selected user input into a new session |
| `/clone` | Copy the complete current active path into a new session |

`/tree` displays the full history tree. Selecting a user input restores its text
in the editor and continues from its parent. Selecting another entry continues
after that entry with an empty editor. Navigation and pending historical input
survive restart. The next model request contains only the selected path.
Idle double Esc with empty input opens the separate `/rewind` checkpoint selector.

`/fork` can select user inputs from inactive branches as well as the active one.
`/fork N` selects the Nth most recently recorded input; `/fork ENTRY` selects an
entry directly. Exact entry IDs take precedence over numeric turn selectors.
The selected input returns to the editor in the new session.
`/clone` clears the editor and copies only the active path, not other branches.
Copies receive new entry IDs and preserve timestamps,
and remap compaction/window references. Navigation and checkpoint controls are
omitted. Copies do not inherit the source's workspace undo stack.

All three operations leave workspace files unchanged. Fork and clone leave the
source session unchanged. They do not implement conversation/file undo and do
not generate an automatic summary of the abandoned branch. Run history changes
only when no task is active.

See the [session schema](reference/session-schema.md) for persistent fields and
[recovery](snapshots-goals.md#checkpoint-recovery) for file restoration boundaries.

## Checkpoint recovery

`/undo` and `/redo` reverse or reapply one action. A root user turn, including
synchronous subagent edits, is one action. Explicit rewind and revert are also
single reversible actions. New actions discard the active redo chain; original
conversation branches remain. Navigation outside the action chain prevents a
stale undo/redo from being applied; use `/rewind` to select the intended point.

`/rewind` restores the position before a selected active-path user prompt and
asks whether to restore conversation, tracked code, or both. `/revert` selects
only code changes over a turn range and file subset. Code-only restoration keeps
conversation messages and adds an audited request-context notice. It does not
rewind provider settings, permissions, credentials, or other host state.

Old or copied turns without owned checkpoints remain conversation-restorable
only. File coverage, conflicts, and interrupted transactions are described in
[Snapshots and goals](snapshots-goals.md#checkpoint-recovery).

## Compaction

When the full conversation exceeds the input budget, `Compactor`:

1. Selects a cut at a visible user boundary.
2. Sends the older messages to the provider for a summary.
3. Appends a `compaction` fact with the summary and `first_kept_id`.
4. Reprojects the conversation as the latest system, summary, and retained tail.

Compaction is iterative: a prior summary is serialized as `PRIOR SUMMARY` and
can be summarized again. The original user, assistant, and tool-result facts
remain in the log.

## Request admission

Request construction preserves the entire projection, including tool outputs.
Only logged compaction and window events reduce visible history. If the request
still exceeds the budget after these steps, the loop returns `context_error`
without sending it to the provider. Use the `history` tool to retrieve evidence
outside the current context.

## Windows

A `window` fact starts a new context at a user entry and may include a handoff.
The TUI can start one explicitly with `/new-context`. If compaction cannot bring
a request under budget, the loop can append an automatic window with a fixed
handoff that points to `NOTE.md` and the history tool.

## History tool

`history` accepts one of:

- `query`: case-insensitive search over the branch, returning entry IDs and
  snippets.
- `entry_id`: exact content of one log entry.
- `call_id`: exact tool result for one call.

Exact content is capped. Search results are capped and point back to entry IDs.

## Request context order

For each task the request contains:

1. The system message.
2. Project instructions from `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or their variants.
3. The skill catalog.
4. `NOTE.md` working state.
5. `MEMORY.md` durable facts.
6. An active goal.

Items 2-6 are request-only context. They are recorded in the request audit but
never become conversation facts. See [Architecture](architecture.md) and the
[design](history/design-proposal.md).

# How Cade works

<!-- source: design/how-it-works.md -->

# How Cade works

Cade coordinates one model request at a time, executes the requested tools,
and records every durable fact in a session log.

## One run

A submitted task is appended as a `user` fact. Cade projects the active
branch, builds a request for the current budget, and sends it to the provider.
The provider streams text and tool calls. The loop records the assistant
message, executes each tool call, and records a tool result. If the model needs
another request, the loop starts another step; otherwise the run ends.

A step is one request plus the tools caused by its response. A run can contain
many steps. The loop stops on completion, a step limit, context exhaustion,
cancellation, or a provider error.

## Context

The projection supplies conversation history. Request-only context supplies
project instructions, the skill catalog, `NOTE.md`, `MEMORY.md`, and an active
goal. Request admission preserves projected tool results and rejects requests
that exceed the budget. The history tool can read original retained facts.

Compaction adds a summary fact and keeps a recent tail. A window moves the
context start forward and may include a handoff. Neither operation rewrites the
original messages.

## Sessions

Sessions are JSONL files under `.cade/sessions`. Entries have IDs and parent
IDs, so a session can form a tree; the active branch ends at the latest entry.
Resuming opens the same file and appends new facts.

## Interfaces

The terminal host runs one task or a TUI. These interfaces call the same loop
and share policy, tools, and session storage with every other entry path.

## Extensions

Skills add on-demand instructions. Memory adds durable facts. MCP adds remote
tools. Subagents run an independent child session. Each extension is a narrow
adapter over the loop, not a change to the session schema.

## Trust and permissions

Every tool call passes through a policy. Modes, static rules, session grants,
shell classification, and approvals decide whether a call runs. Linux/macOS
shell and file tools also use OS confinement; Windows runs directly. See
[Tools and security](../tools-security.md) for scopes and limitations.

See [Architecture](../architecture.md) for the invariant and
[Capability seams](capability-seams.md) for the contracts.

# Code map

<!-- source: design/code-map.md -->

# Code map

Cade is an independent project. The `cade` distribution installs the
`cade` package and the `cade` command. It does not install or depend
on the earlier Cade project.

## Package layout

```text
src/cade/
  ai/                       providers, model protocols, authentication
  harness/
    session/                facts, schema, log, projection, history
    execution/              scope contracts and local execution backends
    loop.py                 log-driven turns and provider retries
    executor.py             shared tool authorization and execution
    tools.py, provider.py   runtime contracts
    request.py              request admission and wire conversion
    compaction.py           summary-based context reduction
    window.py               explicit context window reset
  coding/
    tools/                  read, write, edit, search, bash, history, question
    context/                prompts, instructions, note, memory
    security/               workspace policy, rules, grants, approval, review
    workspace/              snapshots and coordinated recovery
    subagents.py            coding child sessions and delegation tools
    skills/                 discovery, activation, resources, context recovery
    mcp/                    SDK connections, tool discovery, result validation
    mcp_config.py           MCP connection configuration
    goal.py                 workspace goal state and tool
  app/                      bootstrap, active session, config, auth, commands
  hosts/                    CLI and TUI presentation
  docs.py
  __main__.py
tests/            regression and integration tests
```

Provider and execution modules originated in the earlier Cade project and are
now owned and maintained here. Cade includes only the process execution code it
uses, not the earlier project's filesystem or Linux sandbox implementation. Its
own process wrapper uses installed bubblewrap on Linux and Seatbelt on macOS;
Windows runs directly.

## Entry points

```bash
uv run --locked cade
uv run --locked cade exec "Fix the failing test."
uv run --locked python -m cade
uv run --locked cade login
```

The console script and Python module call `cade.hosts.cli:main`. Login
is handled by `cade.hosts.auth`. Credentials and user skills live under
`~/.cade/`. Project sessions and other state live under `.cade/`.
State from the earlier Cade project is not compatible.

## Import direction

- `ai` imports no other Cade layer.
- `harness` imports only itself and `ai`; local execution is internal to it.
- `coding` imports itself, `harness`, and `ai`.
- `app` assembles these lower layers and owns product-level session operations.
- `hosts` call application operations and adapt lower-layer contracts for I/O.

`app.bootstrap.create_session()` is the shared assembly entry point. It accepts
configuration and caller-owned resources without importing terminal modules.
`ApplicationSession.run_task()` serves both one-shot and TUI execution.
`harness.executor.execute_tool()` is the common tool execution boundary.

Configuration types belong to the capability they configure: permission rules
live in `coding/security/rules.py`, and MCP connection settings live in
`coding/mcp_config.py`. `CadeConfig` composes them, so capabilities do not import
application configuration.

`tests/test_architecture.py` enforces package dependencies and execution-contract
isolation. There are no legacy `core`, `execution_env`, `extensions`, `safety`,
or `tools` packages at the Cade root.

The package root has no public re-exports; import the owning submodule
directly.

See [Architecture](../architecture.md),
[How Cade works](how-it-works.md), and
[Capability seams](capability-seams.md) for runtime contracts.

# Relationship to the earlier Cade project

<!-- source: design/cade-comparison.md -->

# Relationship to the earlier Cade project

This repository was previously named Cade Mini. It is separate from the earlier
Cade implementation. It develops, tests, and releases only this Cade
implementation and does not provide compatibility with the earlier project's
Python package, commands, settings, credentials, or session formats.

This project originated as a log-first implementation alongside the earlier
Cade. Its provider adapters and process execution code were brought into the
`cade` package when it became independent. They are no longer shared runtime
dependencies.

## Product boundary

Cade provides a terminal TUI and one-shot execution. Its core separates
append-only session facts, deterministic projection, request admission, and the
run loop.

Intentional limits include:

- No plugin runtime, RPC, or SDK.
- No artifact store or parallel tool scheduler.
- No permanent approval grants; durable rules belong in project config.
- No Windows OS sandbox; Linux uses bubblewrap and macOS uses Seatbelt.

The [historical parity acceptance](../parity.md) records workflows tested
before separation. It is not a promise of future feature parity. See the
[code map](code-map.md) for the current package and ownership boundaries.

# Capability seams

<!-- source: design/capability-seams.md -->

# Capability seams

Cade keeps a small number of explicit contracts. A seam is a place where an
implementation can be replaced without changing the session schema or the loop.

| Seam | Contract | Implementations | Main consumers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Provider | `harness.provider.Provider` streaming events | OpenAI Responses, ChatGPT plan (SIWC), DeepSeek Responses | Loop, compaction, auto-review |
| Tool | `harness.tools.Tool` name, description, parameters, execute | Workspace tools, history, skill, memory, goal, delegate, MCP | Loop |
| Policy | `permissions.Policy.check` returns decision, reason, and scope | `WorkspacePolicy` | Loop, CLI shell |
| Approval | `ApprovalRequest` to `ApprovalResult`, optionally async | `SessionApprover`, `AutoReviewer` | Authorization |
| Execution scope | `ExecutionScope` and `PlatformSandbox.wrap` | bubblewrap, Seatbelt, Windows direct | Workspace tools |
| Compaction | `Compactor(log, budget)` | LLM summary compactor | Loop |
| Session store | `SessionLog` append, branch, open | File-backed JSONL log | Every layer above it |
| Recovery | `WorkspaceRecovery.step` and owned checkpoints | Content-addressed file snapshots and action history | Application, CLI, TUI |
| Application | `ApplicationSession` created by `app.bootstrap.create_session` | Shared application service | CLI and TUI |
| Host | Input, output, and approval adapters over the application | CLI and TUI | Users |

## Provider

The loop needs a streaming event source: text deltas, tool calls, a final
message, usage, and failures. A provider owns wire conversion and replay state.
Cade does not depend on provider-specific message types above this seam.

## Tool

A tool declares a JSON schema and an async `execute`. A tool result is content,
an error flag, and optional metadata. Tools do not write the session log; the
loop records their results.

## Policy and approval

`harness.executor.execute_tool` applies policy and authorization for model and
direct application tool calls. It manages scope, timeout, and errors without
writing session facts. Policy returns a decision, not an execution. Approval is only consulted for
`ask`. A denial becomes a tool error fact, so the model can recover. Keeping
these separate lets the host choose a TTY prompt, a model reviewer, or a
non-interactive denial.

## Stores

`SessionLog` is the durable history. `SnapshotStore`, `GoalStore`, and the
memory and NOTE files are host state, not session facts. Treating them as
separate stores keeps the schema closed while allowing recovery and long-term
state.

## Host

A host owns presentation, input, and the event loop boundary. It does not own
the agent loop or the schema. The CLI renders events and runs tasks without
changing either.

## Tests as contracts

Each seam has a focused test module so a seam cannot quietly become a hidden
dependency.

# Event model

<!-- source: design/event-model.md -->

# Event model

A session is a tree of entries, not a message array. Entry types fall into two
groups.

## Model-visible facts

These entries project into the conversation:

| Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Base system prompt; the latest one wins |
| `user` | User task or steering input |
| `assistant` | Text and tool calls produced by one model response |
| `tool_result` | Result paired to a tool call |
| `compaction` | Summary plus `first_kept_id`; shadows older entries |
| `window` | New context start plus optional handoff |

`compaction` and `window` also carry projections of their own: a summary
message. The original entries remain readable by the history tool.

## Audit facts

These entries never project:

| Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `meta` | Session creation metadata |
| `request` | Provider, model, context, digests, estimated tokens, dropped evidence |
| `attempt` | One provider attempt, including failures and retries |
| `run` | Termination, steps, usage, error |

Audit facts make the request reproducible without turning diagnostics into
conversation. A failed run therefore cannot fabricate an assistant message.

## Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  log[Session log] --> project[Projection]
  project --> conversation[Conversation]
  conversation --> request[Request build]
  request --> provider[Provider stream]
  provider --> facts[Assistant and tool-result facts]
  facts --> log
  request --> audit[request fact]
  provider --> attempts[attempt facts]
  facts --> run[run fact]
```

The loop appends the user fact before the first request. Each step appends one
assistant fact and zero or more tool-result facts. A run appends exactly one
`run` fact.

## Ordering and pairing

A tool result follows its assistant tool call. Projection rejects an orphan
result or a duplicate result. If the branch ends after a tool call without a
result, projection inserts a synthetic interrupted result at the tail so the
request remains protocol-valid.

## Compaction and windows

A compaction cuts at a user boundary. Its summary message appears first in the
retained context. A window discards earlier entries and may insert a handoff.
Only the latest cut applies. Compaction is preferred; a window is a fallback
when a summary cannot fit.

## Schema authority

The closed schema is in [Session log schema](../reference/session-schema.md). The
generated [event catalog](event-catalog.md) lists the current event types from
code.

# Tool execution

<!-- source: design/tool-execution.md -->

# Tool execution

Every tool call follows the same pipeline. Policy and approval decide whether a
call may run. The shared harness executor owns execution, and the loop records
model-turn results. Direct application calls use the same executor without
inventing conversation facts.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  call[Tool call] --> policy[Policy decision]
  policy -->|deny| denied[Denied tool result]
  policy -->|ask| approval[Approval]
  approval -->|deny| denied
  approval -->|allow| execute[Execute tool]
  policy -->|allow| execute
  execute --> result[Tool result]
  result --> log[Append fact]
  denied --> log
```

## Order

1. The model returns a tool call with an ID and arguments.
2. Policy checks tool name, path, mode, rules, grants, and shell classification.
3. An `ask` decision is resolved by the host: TTY prompt, `--yes`, auto-review,
   or denial.
4. The tool executes within the approved per-call scope, with a timeout and
   cancellation token. Linux/macOS workspace tools use OS confinement.
5. The result is truncated, appended as a `tool_result` fact, and rendered.
   Its `artifact.authorization` records decision, reason, and scope without
   adding that metadata to the model transcript.

## Denials and errors

A denied call is not an exception. It becomes an error tool result so the model
can adapt. Unknown tools, malformed arguments, timeouts, and thrown exceptions
also become error results. A cancellation appends interrupted results for any
remaining calls before the run terminates.

## Evidence retention

Model-turn tool results are facts. Request admission preserves projected
messages and rejects an over-budget request rather than replacing old bodies.
Compaction and window events explicitly reduce visible history. The history
tool retrieves exact retained facts by `call_id` or entry ID.

## Tests

- `test_loop.py` covers approval, errors, timeouts, cancellation, retries,
  and window fallback.
- `test_policy.py` covers modes, rules, grants, and boundaries.

See [Tools and security](../tools-security.md) for user-facing behavior.

# Event catalog

Session entry types from `EventType`.

| Event | Projects | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `meta` | No | Session creation |
| `system` | Yes | Base system prompt; latest wins |
| `user` | Yes | Task or steering input |
| `assistant` | Yes | Model text and tool calls |
| `tool_result` | Yes | Tool output paired by call ID |
| `compaction` | Yes | Summary and first kept entry |
| `window` | Yes | Context start and optional handoff |
| `request` | No | Provider request audit |
| `run` | No | Run termination, steps, and usage |
| `attempt` | No | Provider attempt, retry, or failure |
| `branch` | No | Unclassified |
| `checkpoint` | No | Unclassified |
| `restore` | No | Unclassified |

# Tool catalog

<!-- source: design/tool-catalog.md -->

# Tool catalog

The built-in tool surface. MCP tools are discovered at startup and named
`mcp__<server>__<tool>`; their parameters come from the server.

| Tool | Parameters | Side effect | Default policy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `read` | `path`, `offset`, `limit` | None | Allow except protected paths |
| `write` | `path`, `content` | Creates or replaces a file; snapshot first | Ask in ask, allow in build |
| `edit` | `path`, `edits: [{oldText, newText}]` | Applies disjoint replacements against the original file; snapshot first | Ask in ask, allow in build |
| `bash`, `powershell` | `command`, `timeout`, `workdir`, `additional_write_paths` | Arbitrary process; snapshot common mutations | Normal development allowed in build; detected risks ask |
| `question` | `questions: [{question, header, options, multiple?}]` | Collects user answers; dismissal ends the turn | Allow, including plan |
| `websearch` | `query` | Searches through Exa | Allow when network access is enabled |
| `webfetch` | `url`, `format`, `timeout` | Fetches text, Markdown, or HTML | Allow when network access is enabled |
| `history` | `query`, `entry_id`, `call_id`, `limit` | None | Allow |
| `skill` | `name` | None; loads a skill body | Allow |
| `memory` | `text` | Appends to `MEMORY.md` | Allow; denied read-only |
| `goal` | `action`, `objective` | Updates `.cade/goal.json` | Allow |
| `delegate` | `prompt` or `tasks`, `mode`, `description` | Creates one or more child sessions | Allow |
| `mcp__*` | Server-defined | Remote side effects | Ask; denied plan and read-only |

## Reading the table

- "Side effect" is what the tool can change, not what it always changes.
- Workspace `write` and `edit` fail closed if the snapshot cannot be taken.
  External writes require permission and have no workspace snapshot.
- `bash` read-only classification is conservative; unknown commands ask in
  ask mode and are denied in plan. Build permits ordinary development commands.
- MCP tools are dynamic. A rule can allow a specific tool; the default is ask.

## Parameters

The authoritative JSON schemas are built into each tool. This table is a
navigation aid; when it disagrees with the tool schema, the schema wins.

See [the behavior contract](../decisions/0015-tool-behavior-parity.md)
for tool defaults and Cade integration. `read` returns file content without
line-number prefixes and supports image attachments. `offset` and `limit`
are positive integers. Editing uses exact text matching; all edits target the
original file and must be unique and disjoint. Use shell commands for directory
listings, file discovery, and content search.
Shell `timeout` is in seconds and has no default. `bash` uses Bash on Windows;
`powershell` uses PowerShell and is available only on Windows.

There are no standalone `ls`, `find`, or `grep` tools. Search commands use the
shell's output limits, permissions, and sandbox. See [decision 0017](../decisions/0017-shell-search.md).

## Related

- [Tools and security](../tools-security.md)
- [Tool execution](tool-execution.md)
- [Configuration catalog](config-catalog.md)

# MCP reference servers

<!-- source: design/mcp-reference.md -->

# MCP reference servers

Cade uses the official MCP SDK for stdio and Streamable HTTP. See
[MCP](../mcp.md) for supported revisions and capabilities.

## Previously verified servers

| Server | Command | Verified |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Filesystem | `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem <dir>` | Discovery and `read_text_file` |
| Memory | `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory` | Discovery of entity tools |
| Sequential Thinking | `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking` | Discovery of `sequentialthinking` |
| Time | `uvx mcp-server-time` | Discovery and `get_current_time` |
| Fetch | `uvx mcp-server-fetch` | Server starts and lists tools |

On Windows, run npm servers through `cmd /c`:

```json
{
  "mcp_servers": {
    "time": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["mcp-server-time"]
    },
    "fs": {
      "command": "cmd",
      "args": [
        "/c", "npx", "-y",
        "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem",
        "C:/path/to/workspace"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

On POSIX use `npx` directly. The Git server needs its repository flag, for
example `--repository <path>`; pass the exact arguments the server expects.

## Capability boundary

The current integration suite verifies local SDK servers over stdio and HTTP,
including resources, prompts, cancellation, and credentials. The external
servers above were verified with the previous client and have not been rerun
for this SDK migration. Sampling and elicitation are not enabled.

## Policy

MCP tools are named `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. They ask by default, are denied in
plan mode and with `--read-only`, and can be allowed by a rule:

```json
{
  "rules": [
    {"tool": "mcp__time__get_current_time", "decision": "allow"}
  ]
}
```

## Verify

```bash
cade --mode build -p "Use the time MCP tool to get the current time in Asia/Singapore."
```

The log records a `tool_result` with the server's text content. A server process
is closed when Cade exits.

## Related

- [Configuration](../configuration.md)
- [MCP](../mcp.md)
- [Custom MCP server](../cookbook/custom-mcp.md)

# Steering and queueing

<!-- source: design/steering-queue.md -->

# Steering and queueing

The TUI keeps accepting input while a task runs. The UI thread renders events
and handles keys; the bridge runs the task in a worker thread with its own
`asyncio` event loop.

## Current design

```text
prompt_toolkit UI thread
  |  Enter / Alt+S / Alt+Q / Alt+Enter / slash commands
  v
ApplicationSession
  |  steering, pending, cancel
  v
worker thread  --  asyncio.run(run_task)
  |
  v
structured event queue  -->  UI thread
```

- `ApplicationSession.run_task` calls the same `run` loop as one-shot mode.
- `service.steering` holds guidance for the next model step.
- `service.pending` holds follow-up tasks for the next turn.
- `service.cancel` wakes a pending provider stream immediately, even before its
  first output. Tools observe the same cancellation token at their safe points.
- The bridge converts loop events into structured events and queues them for the
  UI thread. The provider stream never blocks key handling.

## Commands during a run

| Input | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` | Use the current busy-input mode: queue, steer, or replace |
| `Alt+Enter` | Append guidance at the next model step |
| `Alt+S` | Append guidance at the next model step, regardless of the `Enter` mode |
| `Alt+Q` | Queue a follow-up task, regardless of the `Enter` mode |
| `/steer TEXT` | Append guidance at the next model step |
| `/queue TEXT` | Queue TEXT as a follow-up task |
| `/queue followup` | Make `Enter` queue a follow-up task |
| `/queue steer` | Make `Enter` append guidance |
| `/queue interrupt` | Make `Enter` stop the task and run the message next |
| `/stop` or `Esc` | Interrupt work and restore undelivered queued input to the editor |
| `Ctrl+C` | Clear the editor without cancelling work; press again within 500 ms to exit |
| `/exit` or `/quit` | Exit the TUI |

A follow-up runs automatically when the current task reaches a terminal state.
Queue order is FIFO, and queued tasks stay in the same session. Explicit Esc or
`/stop` cancellation instead returns undelivered inputs to the editor, so they
do not immediately start another run.

`Alt+S` and `Alt+Q` submit the editor's plain text during a run. Empty input
does nothing. Inputs starting with `/`, `!`, or `$` stay in the editor so the
shortcuts do not reinterpret commands as messages. Menus, forms, and approval
requests take priority over message shortcuts. Press `?` to see the key reference;
the running-task hint also shows both shortcuts.

`/steer` is not a prompt injection into a running provider request. The loop
checks the steering queue before each step, appends a `user` fact with
`source: runtime`, and builds the next request from the projection. This keeps
the session log as the source of truth.

## Session commands

`/new`, `/resume`, `/fork`, `/clone`, `/compact`, and
`/new-context` change session state. Run them when no task is active. During a
run, plain text is queued instead.

## Limits

- File workers finish their current operation before observing cancellation.
  Shell workers signal their child processes. Neither behavior rolls back file
  changes; use snapshots when restoration is needed.
- Steering applies between steps, not inside a provider stream or a running
  tool.
- The one-shot `--steer` flag seeds guidance before the first step. It is not a
  substitute for `/steer` during a run.

## Tests

`test_mid_run_steer_reaches_the_next_provider_request` blocks a tool until the
host delivers guidance, then checks that the next provider request contains the
steering fact.

# Persistence catalog

<!-- source: design/persistence-catalog.md -->

# Persistence catalog

Cade separates durable history from host state. The session log is the
authority for what the model saw and what happened; the other stores have
narrower jobs.

| Artifact | Default location | Owner | Lifetime | Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Session log | `.cade/sessions/session-*.jsonl` | `SessionLog` | Project | Current closed structure |
| Snapshots | `.cade/snapshots/` | `SnapshotStore` | Project | Local index |
| Recovery | `.cade/recovery/` | Recovery coordinator | Workspace | Closed records; action journal and pending plan |
| Goal | `.cade/goal.json` | `GoalStore` | Project | One object |
| Working note | `NOTE.md` | Project | Project | Markdown |
| Memory | `MEMORY.md` | `MemoryTool` | Project | Markdown |
| Instructions | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, overrides | Project | Project | Markdown |
| Skills | `~/.cade/skills`, `.cade/skills` | Discovery | User or project | `SKILL.md` |
| Config | `cade.json` | `CadeConfig` | Project | Pydantic, strict |
| Credentials | `~/.cade/auth.json` | `JsonCredentialStore` | User | Provider credentials |
| SIWC host ID | `~/.cade/host.json` | `load_or_create_host_id` | User | Stable agent host identifier |
| Docs site | `docs/index.html` | Docs tool | Repository | Generated |
| LLM catalogs | `docs/llms*.txt` | Docs tool | Repository | Generated |

## The session log

The log is append-only. It stores model-visible facts and audit
facts in one tree. It is the only artifact needed to reconstruct the
conversation and active history position. Compaction, windows, and branch
navigation are log entries, not rewrites.

## Snapshots

Snapshots are an undo journal for file changes. They cover `write`, `edit`, and
common single-command shell mutations. Capture appends one newline-terminated
record to the JSONL index and syncs it. The index ignores an incomplete tail and
repairs it before the next append; invalid complete records remain errors.
The standalone snapshot undo primitive still replaces the shortened index
atomically. Before/after records and content-addressed blobs remain immutable.
See [Snapshots and goals](../snapshots-goals.md) for conflict and legacy behavior.
Snapshots are not part of the session branch.

## Goals and notes

A goal is one objective with an active or done status. `NOTE.md` is working
state that is included in every request and summarized during compaction.
`MEMORY.md` is durable project knowledge. These files are intentionally plain:
they can be edited by hand and inspected with ordinary tools.

## Generated artifacts

The docs site, `llms.txt`, and `llms-full.txt` are generated from Markdown and
`docs.json`. They are checked for freshness; do not edit the HTML by hand.

## What is not persisted

- Request-only context is recorded in the request audit, not as messages.
- Grants last for the process; durable policy belongs in config rules.
- Approval prompts and TUI state are host state.
- Provider replay payloads live inside the assistant fact that produced them.

See [Session log schema](../reference/session-schema.md) for field-level detail and
[Change policy](../persistence/change-policy.md) for schema changes.

# Glossary

<!-- source: design/glossary.md -->

# Glossary

One canonical term per concept. Links point to the owning page.

## session log

The append-only JSONL file that records facts. It is the source of truth for the
active branch. See [Log](../subsystems/log.md).

## branch

A path through the entry tree. The active branch ends at the latest entry and
supplies the projection.

## projection

The deterministic conversation produced from a branch. It applies the latest
system, compaction, and window cuts, then pairs tool calls with results. See
[Projection and request](../subsystems/projection-request.md).

## request

The admitted, provider-ready form of a conversation for one model call. It
includes tools, budget, and request-only context. A request is not a fact and is
never projected.

## run

One invocation of the loop over a task. A run contains one or more steps and
ends with a `run` fact.

## step

One model request plus the tool calls caused by its response.

## tool result

The recorded output of one tool call, paired by call ID. It is a fact.

## compaction

A fact that adds a summary and a `first_kept_id`. It shadows older messages in
later projections without deleting them.

## window

A fact that moves the context start forward, optionally with a handoff. It is a
fallback when compaction cannot fit.

## history

The tool that retrieves exact evidence by entry ID or call ID after compaction
or pruning.

## mode

`plan`, `build`, or `ask`. A mode selects the default policy for tools and shell
commands.

## rule

A static policy entry in config. Rules can match tool, path prefix, and command
prefix and return allow, deny, or ask.

## grant

A process-local approval created by answering `a`. It matches the same tool and
path or command.

## skill

A `SKILL.md` body loaded on demand. The request carries a catalog; the `skill`
tool loads the body.

## MCP

Model Context Protocol. Cade runs stdio MCP servers and exposes their tools
as `mcp__<server>__<tool>`.

## subagent

A child run with its own session and a restricted tool set. It cannot spawn
another subagent.

## snapshot

A file image retained by the workspace recovery store. Checkpoint actions refer
to before and after images for undo and redo.

## goal

A durable objective in `.cade/goal.json`, separate from the session
schema.

# Testing

<!-- source: design/testing.md -->

# Testing

Tests are grouped by the layer they protect. Run the smallest group that covers
a change, then the full suite before a release.

## Commands

```bash
mkdir -p e2e-results
uv run --locked pytest -q tests --basetemp=e2e-results/pytest
uv run --locked pytest -q tests/test_loop.py --basetemp=e2e-results/pytest
uv run --locked ruff check src/cade/ tests/
uv run --locked ruff format --check src/cade/ tests/
uv run --locked pyright src/cade/
uv run --locked python -m cade.docs check
```

## Coverage map

| Area | Tests |
| --- | --- |
| Sessions | `test_log.py` |
| Projection and pairing | `test_projection.py` |
| Budget, pruning, wire format | `test_request.py` |
| Loop, approvals, retries, windows | `test_loop.py` |
| Provider and auth | `test_provider.py`, `test_auth.py`, `test_siwc_auth.py`, `test_responses_siwc_contract.py` |
| Workspace tools | `test_tools.py` |
| Compaction and windows | `test_compaction.py`, `test_window.py` |
| CLI and config | `test_cli.py`, `test_config.py` |
| Instructions, skills, memory, NOTE | `test_instructions.py`, `test_skills.py`, `test_memory.py`, `test_note.py` |
| Safety and modes | `test_policy.py`, `test_shell.py`, `test_grants.py` |
| Extensions | `test_mcp.py`, `test_subagents.py` |
| Recovery | `test_snapshots.py`, `test_goal.py` |
| Docs | `test_docs.py` |

## Real-provider checks

The acceptance runs use OpenAI Responses with an API key or ChatGPT plan usage
and are not part of the default test suite. They cover tool use, resume,
compaction, skills, build mode, and write/read. Record the command and observed
result in the change that adds a new acceptance.

## Docs checks

`test_docs.py` and `uv run --locked python -m cade.docs check` validate the manifest,
links, anchors, and generated catalogs. The docs job runs in CI.

## Standalone distribution

Build the wheel and source archive with `uv build --no-sources`. Install the
wheel in a clean virtual environment and check both `cade --help` and
`python -m cade --help` outside the source tree. The installed environment must
contain only this distribution's package and command. See the
[validation guidelines](../testing.md).

# Cade session schema

<!-- source: reference/session-schema.md -->

# Cade session schema

> This is the current persistent structure and projection contract.
> Records have no format-version field.

## Envelope

One JSON object per line in `session-<id>.jsonl`:

```json
{"id":"e2","parent":"e1","ts":"2026-10-18T03:00:00+00:00","type":"user","data":{"text":"Fix the test","source":"user"}}
```

| Field | Type | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Unique in the file; 12 lowercase hex characters |
| `parent` | string or null | Previous head normally; selected continuation for navigation; null for a root |
| `ts` | string | ISO 8601 UTC timestamp |
| `type` | string | One of the event types below |
| `data` | object | Type-specific payload |

The head is the last physical event. A normal event points to the previous head.
A `branch` event instead points to a selected historical continuation point.
Other paths remain in the same file. Non-null parents must precede their children.

Unknown event types are invalid. Do not ignore them.

Payloads are validated on append and read. Unknown fields, wrong primitive
types, invalid enums, and non-finite numbers are rejected. Missing optional
fields are allowed but defaults are not written into the record. `user.source`
defaults to `user`; assistant model/provider/usage/replay metadata and nullable
artifact/handoff/usage/details fields may be absent. Cross-event call pairing
and context-cut references are validated by projection.

## Event types

### Conversation events

These produce model-visible messages.

| Type | Payload | Projection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `system` | `{"text": str}` | Latest one is emitted first; never shadowed |
| `user` | `{"text": str, "source": "user"\|"runtime"}` | User message at its position |
| `assistant` | `{"blocks": [Block], "model": str, "provider": str, "usage": object\|null, "provider_state": object\|null, "reasoning": str\|null, "response_metrics": object\|null}` | Assistant message; empty blocks are skipped |
| `tool_result` | `{"call_id": str, "status": "ok"\|"error"\|"interrupted", "content": str, "artifact": object\|null}` | Tool message; paired with its call |
| `compaction` | `{"summary": str, "first_kept_id": str, "tokens_before": int, "model": str, "provider": str, "usage": object\|null, "details": object\|null}` | Emits a summary message, then the tail from `first_kept_id` |
| `window` | `{"start_id": str, "reason": "manual"\|"fallback", "handoff": str\|null}` | Starts the projection at `start_id`; optional handoff summary |

A block is one of:

```json
{"type":"text","text":"..."}
{"type":"tool_call","id":"c1","name":"bash","args":{"command":"pytest -q"}}
```

`assistant.blocks` is the only record of a tool call. Do not add a separate
`tool_use` event. The `tool_result.call_id` pairs with it.

A `provider_state` is opaque adapter data for Responses replay. It is
stored on the assistant fact and passed back to the same adapter. It never enters
the conversation vocabulary.

The harness owns optional `assistant.reasoning` and `assistant.response_metrics`.
`reasoning` contains the provider's streamed reasoning summary. `response_metrics`
contains `ttft_seconds` and `tokens_per_second`, each a nonnegative finite number
or null. TTFT includes the wait for the first nonempty text or reasoning delta.
TPS uses reported output tokens and the interval from that delta to the final
response; failed or cancelled requests have null TPS. These fields remain with
the assistant record for the session's lifetime. They restore host output and
never enter model messages or provider replay data. Failed attempts discarded
for a retry do not become assistant records.

The TUI restores stop notices from `run.termination` and `run.error`, without
storing formatted notices or duplicating answers. See
[decision 0016](../decisions/0016-durable-response-observations.md).

### Log-only events

These are recorded but never projected.

| Type | Payload | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `meta` | `{"session": str, "project": str, "created": str}` | First event; identifies the session |
| `request` | `{"model": str, "provider": str, "tools_digest": str, "conversation_digest": str, "context": [str], "estimated_tokens": int, "dropped": [str], "snapshot": object}` | Request audit with normalized inputs |
| `run` | `{"termination": str, "steps": int, "usage": object\|null, "error": str\|null}` | Run outcome |
| `attempt` | `{"model": str, "provider": str, "error": str, "usage": object\|null}` | Failed model attempt that produced no message |
| `branch` | `{"selected_id": str}` | Navigation control; never a model message |
| `checkpoint` | `{"checkpoint_id": str, "user_id": str, "anchor_id": str\|null, "phase": "started"\|"completed"\|"incomplete"}` | Turn ownership and completion audit |
| `restore` | `{"operation_id": str, "target_id": str\|null, "draft_id": str\|null, "scope": "conversation"\|"code"\|"both", "kind": "undo"\|"redo"\|"rewind"\|"revert"}` | Recovery commit and conversation position |

The `request.snapshot` contains `messages`, `tools`, `options`, `budget`, and
`report`. `budget` records the context window, output reserve, and headroom;
`report` records the admission result. Options omit API keys, all headers,
cancellation signals, and callbacks. This is the provider-interface input, not
an HTTP capture. The remaining request data is not redacted.

A failed attempt does not become an assistant message. A run result does not
duplicate the final answer; the answer is the last assistant text.

Image tools store attachments in `tool_result.artifact.tool_metadata.images`.
Each image has `data` (base64) and `mimeType`. Projection restores these images
alongside the text; request snapshots record them in a tool message's `images`
field. The Responses adapter sends them as `input_image` function output items.
The tool owns the attachment data for the lifetime of the session log.

## Invariants

1. **One fact, one record.** A tool call appears once, in its assistant event.
   The final answer is not stored again.
2. **No derived content.** No replacement message list, no rendered preview used
   as history, no display summary.
3. **Decisions are facts.** A compaction cut and a window start are logged; the
   messages they produce are recomputed.
4. **Request context is audited, not history.** Dynamic context and the request
   envelope live in `request`; only conversation events project.
5. **A compaction cut is a user turn.** `first_kept_id` must name a `user` event
   before the compaction. A tool call and its result never cross the cut.
6. **A window start is a user turn.** `start_id` must name a `user` event before
   the window.
7. **The latest system event wins.** It is projected first and is not shadowed by
   compaction or a window.

## Branch navigation

`branch.selected_id` must reference an earlier entry in the same file. When that
entry is a user input, the navigation event's parent must equal the input's
parent. Otherwise, its parent must equal the selected entry's ID. Selecting a
legacy root user can produce a navigation event with a null parent.

The navigation event becomes the physical head. `branch()` follows its parent
chain to reconstruct the active path. No sibling facts are deleted or copied,
and `project()` ignores navigation records. The latest navigation on the active
path restores selected user text after restart until a subsequent user or
assistant entry consumes it. Non-user selection restores an empty draft. There
is no mutable cursor sidecar.

Navigation and path copying acquire the whole-session run lock. Invalid targets
fail before tail repair or append. Fork and clone copy one connected path into a
new file, omit navigation/checkpoint/recovery controls, preserve timestamps, and
remap entry IDs and context cuts.

## Checkpoints and coordinated recovery

A host lifecycle creates a workspace checkpoint before the user fact. Its
`started` event links the saved checkpoint to that earlier user entry and the
pre-turn ancestor `anchor_id`. A `completed` or `incomplete` event closes the
turn after execution. Completion describes tracked capture, not model success.
The core validates user and ancestor references; file
images and recovery action history belong to the workspace recovery store.

A restore event is appended only after the pending plan's file writes succeed.
Its parent equals `target_id`, which must be an earlier entry or null. Code-only
restoration must target the immediately preceding physical head, preserving
conversation ancestry. `draft_id` is null or an earlier user entry whose text
returns to the editor. New conversation messages consume the historical draft.
If a legacy root restore lacks a system fact, the pending plan supplies the
current system prompt as a new explicit fact before the action is acknowledged.

The workspace action journal and `pending.json` plan use closed models.
A stable operation ID deduplicates
session and action commits after interruption. Unknown external file states stop
recovery and block new writes. See [Checkpoint recovery](../snapshots-goals.md#checkpoint-recovery).

## Projection

`project(branch) -> list[Message]` is pure and deterministic.

1. Find the latest `system` event. Emit it first.
2. Find the latest `window`. If present, start at its `start_id` and keep its
   non-empty `handoff` for a summary message.
3. Find the latest `compaction` at or after the window start. If present, emit
   its summary and start the tail at `first_kept_id`.
4. Walk the retained entries in order. Emit `user`, `assistant`, and
   `tool_result` messages. Skip `system`, `meta`, `window`, `compaction`,
   `request`, `run`, `attempt`, `branch`, `checkpoint`, and `restore`.
5. Pair tool calls with results by call ID.
6. For an open call at the end, synthesize one interrupted result. Do not write
   it to the log. Insert it after the assistant message that contains the call.
7. Reject an orphan result, a duplicate result, a duplicate call, a bad cut, or a
   bad window with `ProjectionError`.

Order of emitted summary messages: system, window handoff, compaction summary,
retained tail.

The wire adapter renders `SummaryMessage` as a user-role message wrapped in
`<compaction-summary>` or `<window-handoff>`. The internal role stays distinct so
hosts can render it differently.

## Storage

- Directory: `.cade/sessions/` by default.
- File: `session-<id>.jsonl`.
- New interactive sessions defer file creation until the first user or assistant
  message. Setup events stay in memory and are flushed with that message.
  A cancelled first request still keeps its user message on disk.
- Append lock: `session-<id>.lock`.
- Run lock: `session-<id>.run.lock`; concurrent turns are rejected.
- Append: one line, `flush`, `fsync`.
- Before append: truncate an incomplete trailing line from a crash.
- On read: ignore an incomplete trailing line; reject any earlier invalid line.
- Reject duplicate IDs and forward parent references.
- No rewrite, no in-place edit.

## Compaction record

```json
{"id":"e80","parent":"e79","ts":"...","type":"compaction",
 "data":{"summary":"## Goal\n...","first_kept_id":"e52","tokens_before":48210,
         "model":"gpt-5.6-luna","provider":"chatgpt",
         "usage":{"input":43000,"output":1200},"details":null}}
```

The summary is model-generated content and must be logged. The original events
before `first_kept_id` stay in the log. A later compaction starts after the
previous one and may include the previous summary in its input.

## Window record

```json
{"id":"e90","parent":"e89","ts":"...","type":"window",
 "data":{"start_id":"e88","reason":"manual","handoff":"Optional note."}}
```

A window is the hard fallback. Compaction is the default. A window is explicit
through `/new-context`, or automatic when compaction cannot reduce enough.

## Development changes

There is one current structure, with no format-version field, compatibility
reader, or migration layer. Breaking changes update producers, readers, tests,
and documentation together. See [Change policy](../persistence/change-policy.md).

# Subsystems

# Subsystems

Each page owns one subsystem's types, behavior, and failure modes. The
[architecture](../architecture.md) is the map; these pages are the reference.

- [Log](log.md): append, lock, branch, list, and repair.
- [Projection and request](projection-request.md): deterministic context and
  budget admission.
- [Loop](loop.md): provider calls, tools, approvals, retries, and facts.
- [Tools and policy](tools-policy.md): workspace tools, modes, rules, grants,
  shell classification, approvals.
- [Context and compaction](context-compaction.md): summaries, windows, history,
  and request context.
- [Extensions](extensions.md): skills, memory, MCP, subagents, snapshots, goals,
  and hosts.

A subsystem page describes current behavior. Historical decisions belong in
[decision records](../decisions/README.md) and incidents in
[postmortems](../postmortem/README.md).

# Log

<!-- source: subsystems/log.md -->

# Log

`SessionLog` owns the append-only JSONL file.

## Create and open

- `SessionLog.create(directory, session_id=None)` creates a unique file and
  writes a `meta` entry.
- `SessionLog.open(path)` validates envelopes, payloads, and
  navigation references. Reads ignore a
  torn final line; the next valid append truncates that tail.
- The session ID is derived from the file name when not supplied.

## Append

`append(type, data)`:

1. Validates the payload without modifying the file.
2. Takes an exclusive file lock.
3. Checks file identity, size, and nanosecond timestamps. Reuses validated
   entries when unchanged; otherwise reloads and validates the complete file.
4. Builds an entry and validates its parent and references against the verified
   ID index, then repairs a torn tail only after validation succeeds.
5. Appends one JSON line, flushes, and calls `fsync`.
6. Releases the lock.

`fsync` is deliberate: a returned append is durable enough to resume. A failed
write raises an error and does not return a fake entry.

The cache is private and updated only after a successful write and sync. Another
writer, file replacement, or truncation invalidates it when file metadata changes.
`entries()` and `branch()` return independent copies, including nested payloads.
The cache adds no durable state and does not change request audits.

`run_lock()` protects a whole turn separately from individual appends. It rejects
competing operations immediately with `LogError`. `run()`, manual CLI context
changes, navigation, and path copying use it; other multi-event storage clients
must acquire it explicitly.

## Branch

`branch()` follows parent IDs from the last entry back to the root and reverses
the list. `branch(entry_id)` reads the path ending at a historical entry. Reads
reject cycles, missing parents, duplicate IDs, and invalid navigation targets.

`switch_branch(selected_id)` appends a navigation event in the same file.
User selection continues before that input and exposes its text through
`navigation_draft`; other selection continues after the entry with an empty
